done.why: The trap door locked behind me, every other way out of the cellar area was blocked or unfinished, and I had found no treasure.

about: A changed Zork. You start outside the white house, go in through the window, take a lantern, sword and sack, and go down into the cellar. The troll dies in one blow, but the passages beyond are unfinished and I never found any treasure.

moments.note: After 'take the leaflet and read it' the game said it couldn't see any such thing, even though I had just opened the mailbox and the leaflet was inside.
The troll died in one sword blow and its body vanished in black fog.
The east passage is 'not finished' and has a note from the Management pinned to the rock.
The trap door is locked behind me, so I can't go back up and I'm trapped in a small area.

wished: Get past the unfinished passages and find a treasure.
Get back up through the trap door.
Know what the sack was for.

lines.line: The passage to the east has not been finished. A note is pinned to the rock: "Back soon. -- The Management."
lines.why: It told me plainly that the world was incomplete and that I'd reached the edge of it.

lines.line: From somewhere beyond it comes the sound of digging, which stops, politely, until you have backed out.
lines.why: A charming line that hints at something happening beyond the blocked crawlway.

fun.why: The opening was pleasant, but I ran out of places to go almost at once.

engagement.why: I was curious at first, then boxed in with nothing to find.

difficulty.why: I couldn't progress at all because every exit was blocked and the trap door locked.

interestingness.why: It's a familiar house with changes, such as the troll dying at once and the unfinished passages, but I saw very little of it.

prose.why: The text is familiar and clear, with a few witty lines in the blocked passages.
